countries.capitalReason: Thamiel, the hill, is the household's hall on a rise in the Kingdom Forests above the pass road, near the graves that kept the household in the west, and from it the guides can see every traveller who comes up from the gorge.
countries.today: Dunelaeth in 4A 1748 is one elven household of some 5,000 under its Eldest, Velaeth, outside the Concord, living in the Kingdom Forests and guiding travellers on the road to the Kingson Pass. It is the only elven realm on the Middle Lands side of the range, and the Kindred Song is sung there in an old western form the eastern elves find quaint.

divergence.what: The household answers Herrodon at last and goes east over the pass.
divergence.consequence: The Kingdom Forests are left without guides, and the elves of the Magical Lands gain a household that knows every way men use through the mountains.

divergence.what: The Eldest guides an army over the Lunhrim Notch in the war, for the heir or against him.
divergence.consequence: A host comes through a pass that admits only raiders, and the household chooses a side in a war of men for the first time since the Staying.

countries.name: Aenor Forest

founding.story: The Baelim say that Graulvoa, the oldest stand of their forest, was already standing when the sea first reached the north coast, and the Selen rangers who live round the forest have no story older than the Baelim's low voices in the wood. The great wet forest between Selen, Konori and the Bloody Forest has never been cut, never had a crown and never let a man build in it; the year is only the rangers' guess at the oldest stand, and the Baelim answer questions about years with silence.

dynasties.name: The Eldest of Graulvoa
dynasties.notable: The Baelim are named for their stands and their stands for their oldest tree; the Eldest of the oldest stand speaks for the whole forest in its slow moot, and nobody outside has ever heard the moot end. Men call the present Eldest Goarvom.

events.name: The Burnt Edge
events.summary: Redbark raiders set fire to the forest's eastern edge to drive game; the Baelim come out of the wood and pull down the raiders' camp trees, and the Redbark have not lit a fire in the forest since.

events.name: The Cutters Who Did Not Return
events.summary: The Order sends woodcutters to take the forest's giant conifers for its forts; none of them come back, and the Order does not send more.

events.name: The Baelim Speak
events.summary: Selen rangers on the forest edge hear the Baelim's voices for nine nights running after a great storm brings down part of a stand; the moots send a ranger in with an offering of water, and the voices stop.

rivalries.nature: The Redbark hunt at the forest's eastern edge and remember the Burnt Edge; the Baelim remember it too.

countries.capitalReason: Baeldran, the old tree, is Graulvoa, the oldest stand of the forest, where the Eldest stands; the Baelim did not choose a seat, they grew one, and men named it.
countries.today: The Aenor Forest in 4A 1748 is a forest domain without a crown, the largest forest of the Middle Lands and home of some 1,500 Baelim, a slow tree-people unlike the ents of Kilinti, who never share a forest with them. No men live inside it; tzikor flower in its clearings, and Selen's rangers leave water at its edge in dry summers.

divergence.what: An army cuts or burns the forest's edge in the war.
divergence.consequence: The Baelim come out of the wood as they did against the Redbark, slowly and without mercy, and the army learns why no road has ever been made through the north coast.

divergence.what: The Baelim let the people of the Selen edge shelter under the stands when the dead come from the north.
divergence.consequence: The largest forest of the Middle Lands becomes a refuge, and the Baelim speak to men in the moot for the first time anyone remembers.

countries.name: Cursed Lands

founding.story: When Aen's victory ended the War of Men, the Orran-speaking houses that would not kneel to the One Crown withdrew into the grey downs east of the Vale with their cord-mothers, their names knotted on the cords and their tongue. The downs were poor but not yet sour, and the Veiled, as the Vale called them for the hoods their women wore, refused every crown that came after; the land was named the Cursed Lands only after the Black Roots soured it in the Third Age.

dynasties.name: The Cord-Mothers of Morluma
dynasties.notable: The Veiled are ruled by a council of cord-mothers, each keeping the eldest cord of her line, and descent runs through mothers; the Mother of the Eldest Cord speaks for the council. Izkala, daughter of Pelzen, keeps the eldest cord in 4A 1748.

events.name: The Withdrawal
events.summary: The Orran houses that refuse the One Crown withdraw into the grey downs and the Bloody Forest; the Veiled and the Redbark have counted the same tie as their first since then.

events.name: The Last Cord Laid
events.summary: At the Withdrawal the cord-mothers carry the cord of the old moot into the eldest barrow of the grey downs, and the Veiled keep its count on the Old Tallies from then on.

events.name: The Revolt of the Hoods
events.summary: In the long weakening the Veiled raid the Vale's eastern roads for a generation, and the crown gives up trying to tax the downs.

events.name: The Souring
events.summary: The Black Roots reach the grey downs and the Necromancer's attempt to turn the land's magic sours the ground for ever; the Veiled stay, learn to grow roots and mushrooms in the sour earth, and the Vale names the land cursed.

events.name: The Charters Refused
events.summary: The cord-mothers refuse the Charters of Parim, as they refused every crown before; Harion lets them alone, since the land is not worth an army.

events.name: The Grey March
events.summary: A Concord host marches into the downs to bring the Veiled under charter and turns back after a summer of poisoned wells and empty villages; no host has tried since.

rivalries.nature: The Veiled have rejected the crown since the Peace of the One Crown; the Grey March of 4A 1310 is their proudest tie.

countries.capitalReason: Morluma is the cord-hall deep in the sour ground where no road reaches, chosen because it is the one place on the downs a Concord host would starve before it arrived.
countries.today: The Cursed Lands in 4A 1748 are a council of cord-mothers over some 40,000 Veiled on sour grey badlands, outside the Concord and against it. They speak Orran among themselves, count the years by the ties of the eldest cord, and trade roots and mushrooms at the downs' edge for iron and salt.

divergence.what: The cord-mothers tie the returned heir's name into the eldest cord.
divergence.consequence: For the first time since the Withdrawal the Veiled stand with a king of Aen's line, and their knowledge of the sour ground opens a road the dark does not watch.

divergence.what: The cord-mothers open the downs to the hosts of the south against the crown that has never let them be.
divergence.consequence: The southern host gains a road round the Vale's eastern flank, and the Veiled learn too late what their new friends think of the living.

countries.name: Bloody Forest

founding.story: The Orran houses that refused the One Crown and went north rather than to the downs took to the great red-oak forest above the Konorar, where the bark bleeds red when it is cut. There the Redbark clans have lived ever since by hunting and dyeing leather, ruled by their cord-mothers in peace and by war-chiefs on raids, and they have never taken a charter from any king.

dynasties.name: The Clan Moot of Giritren
dynasties.notable: The clans of the Redbark meet at the moot-clearing under the oldest red oak, and the cord-mothers of the clans choose a war-chief for each raid and unmake him when it ends. Tzorek, son of Amaz, is the moot's war-chief in 4A 1748 for a feud that has run three summers.

events.name: The First Cord-Tree
events.summary: Orran houses driven east by the sea hang their mothers' cords in the red oaks of the forest, and the forest keeps the beast-clans and the old tongue long after the valleys forget them.

events.name: The Withdrawal North
events.summary: The northern Orran houses go into the red-oak forest and tie the first tie of the Redbark cords; their kin the Veiled go into the downs.

events.name: The Burnt Edge
events.summary: Redbark hunters fire the edge of the Aenor Forest to drive game, and the Baelim pull down their camp trees; the clans have not hunted in that forest since.

events.name: The Dead in the Red Oaks
events.summary: The Order's dead come into the forest and do not come out; the Redbark tell that their cord-trees hold the names of the dead, and that the Necromancer could not raise what was already counted.

events.name: The Red Winter
events.summary: A Redbark raid burns three Selen glade villages, the rangers burn the cord-trees at the forest's rim, and the feud runs until the cord-mothers and the Wardens exchange hostages in the spring.

rivalries.nature: Raid and counter-raid at the forest edge since the First Age; the Red Winter of 4A 1608 is the feud both sides still name.
The Burnt Edge of 2A 1120 is remembered by the Redbark as a lesson and by the Baelim as a debt.

countries.capitalReason: Giritren is the moot-clearing under the oldest stand of red oak, where the clans' cord-trees stand and where every Redbark cord was first knotted; the clans live scattered and meet there only for the moot.
countries.today: The Bloody Forest in 4A 1748 is a clan moot of some 90,000 Redbark under their cord-mothers, outside the Concord and against it. They hunt red deer and boar, dye leather, smuggle along the Organ Coast Road and raid the Selen edge when the moot's war-chief needs a name.

divergence.what: The clans guide raiders or an army along the Organ Coast Road beneath the cliffs at low tide.
divergence.consequence: A road that admits only single files at low water carries war into the north of the Vale, and the Redbark get the price they ask from whoever pays it.

divergence.what: The cord-mothers make peace with Selen's moots when the dead come from the north.
divergence.consequence: The oldest feud of the Middle Lands ends in the war, and the forest's hunters join the rangers against something that cannot be tied into any cord.

cities.name: Parim
cities.legend: The bargemen say the bluff was an Orran ford-town before the War of Men, and that the oldest stones of the lower quays still carry Orran marks; the Stone Forest north of the city, they add, is the wood that heard Aen's last horn and stood still, which is why it creaks in a lake fog.
cities.economy: The crown, the Royal Council, the Concord courts, the University of Parim and the Golden Court; grain barges, lake shipping, cloth, glass, books and the sale of offices.

cities.name: Dolepar
cities.legend: Lake sailors hold that Dolepar's deep bay was dug by Aen's hand in a single night so that his ships would never wait on the weather, and the shipwrights still cast a nail into the water before every launching.
cities.economy: The best deep-water harbour of the lake's south lobe; shipyards, the lake fleet and the grain trade to Safeton.

cities.name: Silesire
cities.legend: Where the Great River comes out of the Kingson gorge into the east lobe, the grain-merchants say the river brings everything down from the mountains but news, which always arrives a week late.
cities.economy: Grain port for the Vale's east, the range trade from Kingson, corallus-wardens in the reeds.

cities.name: Kerepael
cities.legend: Edran built the road fortress where the east road leaves the plain for the gorge, and the garrison still sounds a horn at dusk that, the soldiers say, Edran ordered blown until a king of Aen's line came back to stop it.
cities.economy: Garrison town of the east road, wagon yards, the crown's armoury for the eastern dominions.

cities.name: Grafas
cities.legend: The grey ford under the Grano hills where giants once waded across the lake shallows with stone on their backs; the townsfolk keep a giant's footprint in the quay paving and charge travellers to stand in it.
cities.economy: The west-shore lake port; giant-cut stone from Hirolon, wool and cheese from the Hilofrim herders.

cities.name: Hifeco
cities.legend: Under the Moot Tree beside the town Edran was crowned while the capital lay in enemy hands, and the rangers say the oak has not dropped a leaf on a moot day since.
cities.economy: Moot-house of the Weald, the University of Selen, timber and hunting, the ranger companies' musters.

cities.name: Deolofson
cities.legend: The town takes its name from the son of Deolof, the first Pass-Lord, who held the gorge alone for a night when the Order's last host came back for its forts; the vale reads his name first at every Reading of Names.
cities.economy: The only market inside the range: elven silver, herbs and dragon-scale west, iron, grain and glass east; the pass tolls.

cities.name: Torunalos
cities.legend: The High Chief's hall stands above the cairn-fields on the hill from which every crest of the ring can be seen, and the giants say a chief who cannot see the whole ring from his door has no business being chief.
cities.economy: The giants' hall, the cairn-keepers, cattle that haul stone, the harvest-share brought up from Tirlan.

cities.name: Ulmaros
cities.legend: The harbour at the Hilorn mouth was rebuilt after the sea-orcs burned it, under a beacon-cairn the giants raised in a single night; fishermen say the cairn is the only lighthouse in Aoaz that has never needed a fire.
cities.economy: The ring's only landing: fish, trade with Aenor Isle across the Inner Sea.

cities.name: Hilofrim
cities.legend: The herders tell that a giant once carried a whole flock over the Grano Saddle in a winter storm and asked only for the bell of the lead ram, which hangs over the market cross to this day.
cities.economy: Herders' market at the Grano Saddle; wool, cheese and hides; the House of the First Light that serves the herders.

cities.name: Tirbur
cities.legend: The small folk say the morning fog that lies over Tirbur's fields is the giants' breath, laid over the valleys at night to keep the soil soft and the strangers out.
cities.economy: The moot-place of the three valleys; barley, beans, orchards, honey, beer and a dried smoking herb.

cities.name: Arrovez
cities.legend: At the ford of the Aenar the Hundreds raise their kings on the white felt, and the riders say a king who is set down from the felt must cross the ford on foot and never ride it again.
cities.economy: Horse fairs, remounts for the Concord, the king's felt-hall, the ford toll.

cities.name: Ulrono
cities.legend: The Gathering ground is mostly tents and empties every autumn, and the riders say the stone halls in its middle were built by a Horse-Lord who was tired of losing his hall to the wind.
cities.economy: The summer Gathering, the largest horse fair in Aoaz, the horse-barrows of the downs.

cities.name: Hungohon
cities.legend: On the tower wall hangs the helmet of the warren-boss who broke the Lamp Truce, and the Guard's children are told that it shakes on the nights the goblins dig.
cities.economy: The South Pass garrison, the pilgrim escorts and their fees, farming for the sworn company.

cities.name: Hugomon
cities.legend: Hezar built the fort where the southern road enters the Grey Hills, and the march-folk say his towers face south because he was the only man in the Alliance who expected the war to come back.
cities.economy: March fort and garrison, sheep and barley of the Grey Hills, the southern road's trade.

cities.name: Saelori
cities.legend: The Oath of Eight Hearths was sworn at Saelori's fair-ground over eight fires, and the confederacy still lights eight fires on the first night of every fair so that no town can say its hearth was forgotten.
cities.economy: The fairs of Saelori, toll-free trade, the confederacy's treasury.

cities.name: Ollolor
cities.legend: The moot-grove has no walls and no houses; the edge-folk say that a man who sleeps in it wakes a year older and a word wiser, and so nobody sleeps there.
cities.economy: No trade of its own; the Ent-Moot every seventh spring, and the edge-folk's offerings of water.

cities.name: Lotrenri
cities.legend: Where the lake water meets the sea at the Safen mouth, the ship-houses say a drop of the Great Lake reaches every coast of Aoaz, and their captains pour a cup of lake water into the sea on every outward voyage.
cities.economy: Warehouses, grain shipping, the pilgrim fleet south, shipbuilding.

cities.name: Hordorton
cities.legend: The warm spring of Hordorton rose, the Bowl-Bearers say, where Sulethe set down her bowl to rest on the road, and they still break a bowl on the spring-house threshold when a fever leaves the town.
cities.economy: Spring-houses and hospitals, drovers' inns, the crossing of the lake road and the south road.

cities.name: Horlomon
cities.legend: The guild-hall bell was the first thing cast in Horlomon, before the guild-hall had a roof, and the bell-founders say the town grew up round the sound of it.
cities.economy: Bells, glass, cloth, paper, books and ships; the guild library.

cities.name: Borrak
cities.legend: The queens are chosen in the tide-chamber at the harbour's mouth at the turn of the tide, and the isle's grandmothers say a queen chosen on a falling tide will rule a short time and a hard one.
cities.economy: The isle's fleet, the shipwrights who build with Verde's timber, fishing, the tide-chambers.

cities.name: Deoreh
cities.legend: The toll-chain at Deoreh has been broken three times in four ages, and each time the strait-folk melted the broken links into the chain's new anchor, which is why they say the chain grows heavier every century.
cities.economy: The strait toll, toll-boats, ferries and Leren timber.

cities.name: Hrakkerm
cities.legend: The iron fort at the foot of the Western Gate is where the clans weigh their iron before it goes down to Kingson, and the dwarves say a man who argues with the scales will be told the weight of his own head.
cities.economy: The hold's outer hall and market; iron, gold and gems; the Iron Charter's weighing-house; black powder for the crown.

cities.name: Glimzig
cities.legend: The throne-cave's lamp has never gone out since the first warband lit it, and the goblins say a warren lives as long as its lamp burns, which is why the king's lamp has the best guards in the mountain.
cities.economy: Mining, trapping, salvage and the sale of whatever falls into the tunnels; fire-pots and crude powder.

cities.name: Tovodor
cities.legend: Nobody in Parim has ever seen Tovodor, but the masons' guild tells apprentices that a gnome door in the Stendorler stone leads there, and that the luck of the man who leaves it shut lasts three generations.
cities.economy: Gold mining, hidden gardens, and the luck the gnomes give for gold freely brought.

cities.name: Thamiel
cities.legend: The household's hall stands above the graves that kept it in the west, and the elves say that every traveller they guide over the pass road is shown the graves first, so that he knows why the guides stayed.
cities.economy: Guiding on the road to the Kingson Pass, paid in salt and silver by the forts; forest crafts.

cities.name: Baeldran
cities.legend: Graulvoa, the oldest stand, is where the Eldest stands, and the Selen rangers say the moss under it is warm in winter and that the low voices of the stand can be heard there on still nights.
cities.economy: None; the rangers leave water at the forest edge in dry summers.

cities.name: Morluma
cities.legend: The cord-hall stands where the first cord-mothers knotted the names of the Withdrawal, and the Veiled say that whoever cuts a tie in the eldest cord loses his name in every cord in the downs.
cities.economy: Roots and mushrooms of the sour ground, cord-weaving, trade at the downs' edge for iron and salt.

cities.name: Giritren
cities.legend: The oldest stand of red oak bleeds red when it is cut, and the Redbark say it bled for the first time on the day the clans came into the forest, as a welcome or a warning, nobody agrees which.
cities.economy: Hunting, leather dyed with red-oak bark, smuggling on the Organ Coast Road.

figures.name: Harion of Selen
figures.role: First king of the restored crown
figures.biography: A Warden's son of the Weald and of a collateral branch of Aen's line, Harion spent his youth in the War of Unbinding and held the lake port beneath the Parim bluff for Selen's companies. Crowned at Parim in 4A 1, he rebuilt the roads and granaries, gave the dominions the Charters of Parim and chartered the Houses of the First Light because they had kept the Vale fed; he is called the Restorer in every chronicle.

figures.name: Hezar of Hugomon
figures.biography: A lake-house captain who brought his company home alive from the Ember Lands campaign, Hezar was given the new march across the Grey Hills by Edran in 2A 12 and built its first towers facing south. The march-folk remember him as the only man in the Alliance who expected the war to come back.

figures.name: Ostvar of Deoreh
figures.role: Founder of the toll-lordship of Fotan
figures.biography: A Leren sea-captain who married into the Aenoran ferry-house at the strait's narrowest crossing, Ostvar stretched the first toll-chain across the landing at Deoreh and made the Order's tribute ships pay to pass. The Order burned his tower twice; he rebuilt it twice, and his house has held the strait ever since.

figures.name: Deolof
figures.biography: A head of the watch-families who opened the gorge forts to the Unbinding's companies in 3A 1244, Deolof became the first Pass-Lord under the Pass Charter of 4A 3 and had the forts' names read at the gorge every year. His son's night alone in the gorge gave the vale's town its name.

figures.name: Klungor
figures.role: First Captain of the Klungori Guard
figures.biography: Grandson of a captain of the Unbinding's last company, Klungor took the western foot of the South Pass for land instead of pay with two hundred sworn men and founded the company that still bears his name; he swore the Lamp Truce for it in 4A 96.

figures.name: Saelor of Dalvis
figures.role: First Chief Speaker of the Eight Towns
figures.biography: A toll-master of Dalvis who ended the two-summer toll war of the south-eastern roads by persuading the eight towns to swear one confederacy at Saelori in 4A 774, Saelor laid down the rule that no family holds the Chief Speaker's office twice running.

figures.name: Tamric Bellaren
figures.role: Master of the bell-founders in the Bell Riot
figures.biography: Master of Horlomon's bell-founders when the crown doubled the tax on bells, Tamric rang every bell in the guild-city for three days and nights in 4A 1610 until the Royal Council rescinded it; the guild-hall bell still rings his name on the riot's anniversary.

figures.name: Hallec of the Gate
figures.role: Pass-Lord of Kingson in the Toll of Silver
figures.biography: The Pass-Lord who doubled the toll on elven silver in 4A 1689 and so earned the vale a winter of elven silence, Hallec signed the Kingson Reckoning in 4A 1690 that halved it again; the vale remembers him as clever, the elves as greedy.

lawsAndCustoms.name: The Peace of the One Crown
lawsAndCustoms.summary: No lord of Aenor may make war on another without the crown's judgement; breaking the Peace is the first meaning of rebellion in Aenoran law, and the Concord courts still cite it in every border quarrel.

lawsAndCustoms.name: The twenty-six charter-seats
lawsAndCustoms.summary: The Charters of Parim gave each dominion seats in the Concord Council in proportion to the levies it owed the common defence, twenty-six in all, and a dominion that joins a neighbour keeps the neighbour's seat. In 4A 1748 Selen and Noleksun hold three each; Konori, Hunhun, Kingson, Herez, Kilinti, Safeton, Freshon, Pazoma and Orohaf two each; the Klungori Guard and Kunhrim one each.

lawsAndCustoms.name: The Quiet Law
lawsAndCustoms.summary: No ranger draws a bow on another ranger, no standing tree is felled without the moot's leave, and every stranger is given one night's shelter before he is asked his business.

lawsAndCustoms.name: The Reading of Names
lawsAndCustoms.summary: Every year at the pass forts the names of those who held the passes against the Order are read aloud, and every watch-family's child is presented at the reading in the year it is born.

lawsAndCustoms.name: The Old Promise and the harvest-share
lawsAndCustoms.summary: The small folk carry a share of every harvest up to the giants' halls, and no stranger enters the Hilorn valleys without a giant's leave; the giants say the promise is theirs to keep and not a god's.

lawsAndCustoms.name: The cairn count
lawsAndCustoms.summary: A giant leaves one stone on a cairn for each winter of life, and a dispute between clans is judged by which party can name the older cairn; no giant is ever asked how many stones are in his own.

lawsAndCustoms.name: The Iron Charter
lawsAndCustoms.summary: The hold sells iron to the crown and keeps every elf off its roads, and since 4A 1612 its black powder, made by an art learned from the western hold of Hrennost, goes to the crown and to nobody else.

lawsAndCustoms.name: The Lamp Truce
lawsAndCustoms.summary: Sworn over a lit lamp in 4A 96: the goblins keep the caves, the dwarves the galleries, and nobody crosses into the other's dark; the lamp is relit at the Hungohon tower whenever the truce is renewed.

lawsAndCustoms.name: The Tide-Oath
lawsAndCustoms.summary: The queen is chosen from the daughters of the five Isle Houses by their eldest women, inheritance runs through daughters, and every house gives its dead to the tide by the same rite.

lawsAndCustoms.name: The raising on the felt
lawsAndCustoms.summary: A King of Konori is lifted on a white felt by the heads of the Hundreds at the ford of Arrovez, and a king who loses their trust is set down on it.

lawsAndCustoms.name: The cords of the mothers
lawsAndCustoms.summary: Among the Veiled and the Redbark descent runs through mothers, names are knotted on the mother's cord at birth, and a stolen name is a cut tie; the years are counted by the ties of the eldest cord.

lawsAndCustoms.name: The Golden Charters
lawsAndCustoms.summary: Privileges sold by the Golden King: freedom from royal tolls and a town court of its own, bought by Freshon in 4A 1731 and Pazoma in 4A 1734 at prices that left both in the Golden Court's debt.
